subject.title: doctor --fix migrates codex/gpt-5.5 to openai/gpt-5.5, then Codex app-server startup times out on 2026.6.1

question: Should doctor retain legacy Codex routes unless a migration plan proves the canonical `openai/*` plus Codex runtime path is safe, or should it keep unconditional canonicalization and rely on startup/runtime fixes?
rationale: Both directions touch compatibility-sensitive doctor, auth-provider, and runtime behavior, and current evidence shows open candidate PRs for different halves of the failure rather than one merged owner-approved fix.

options.title: Land guarded migration plan
options.body: Review and land the shared migration-plan approach, then decide whether the startup-timeout PR is also required before this issue can close.

options.title: Keep unconditional canonicalization
options.body: Accept the existing doctor policy but require live macOS/Codex proof that the migrated route no longer times out before closing this issue.

options.title: Split the remaining work
options.body: Make one canonical issue own doctor migration policy and one own Codex startup timeouts, then close only after this combined report is fully covered by those merged outcomes.

recommendation.title: Land guarded migration plan
recommendation.body: Review and land the shared migration-plan approach, then decide whether the startup-timeout PR is also required before this issue can close.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing candidate for the OpenAI provider unification and current Codex runtime direction, while vincentkoc remains a close code-path owner for doctor repair details.
